comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and MU explicitly link the growth in end-user device markets (smartphones for QCOM, PCs for MU) to the integration of AI capabilities. QCOM estimates low-to-mid-single digit growth in smartphone volumes driven by 5G adoption, while MU highlights that next-generation PCs feature AI capabilities and neural processing chipsets, leading to significantly higher DRAM content. Both disclosures identify the shift toward AI-enabled devices as a key driver of demand in their respective consumer segments.

sentences.text: For calendar year 2024, we estimate that consumer demand for 3G, 4G, and 5G handset volumes will increase by a low-to-mid-single digit percentage relative to calendar year 2023.
This estimate includes expected high single-digit to low double-digit percentage growth in 5G handsets.
The next generation PCs that have been announced contain high-performance neural processing chipsets as well as AI.
We expect these devices will have significantly more DRAM content than today's average PC.
